# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 15
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
22 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-he-walked in-all the-sins-of his-father that he-did before-him, and-his-heart was-not complete with YHWH his-God, like-the-heart-of David his-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** And he walked in all the sins that his father did before him, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as the heart of David his father.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He committed all the same sins his father had committed before him. His heart was not fully devoted to the LORD his God, as David his ancestor's heart had been.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 4
**EMET (literal):** For for-the-sake-of David, YHWH his-God gave to-him a-lamp in-Jerusalem, to-raise-up ʾet-his-son after-him and-to-establish ʾet-Jerusalem,

**LOGOS (formal):** Nevertheless, for David's sake the LORD his God gave him a lamp in Jerusalem, setting up his son after him and establishing Jerusalem,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** But for David's sake, the LORD his God kept a lamp burning for him in Jerusalem by raising up a son to succeed him and by keeping Jerusalem secure.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** because David did the-right in-the-eyes-of YHWH and-did-not turn-aside from-all that he-commanded-him all the-days-of his-life — except in-the-matter-of Uriah the-Hittite.

**LOGOS (formal):** because David did what was right in the eyes of the LORD and did not turn aside from anything that he commanded him all the days of his life, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** David had done what was right in the LORD's eyes and had never failed to obey any of the LORD's commands throughout his life — except in the incident involving Uriah the Hittite.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** And-war was between Rehoboam and-Jeroboam all the-days-of his-life.

**LOGOS (formal):** Now there was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** There was war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam throughout Abijam's life.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** And-Abijam lay-down with his-fathers, and-they-buried-him in-the-City-of David. And-Asa his-son reigned in-his-place.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Abijam slept with his fathers, and they buried him in the city of David. And Asa his son reigned in his place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Abijam died and was buried in the City of David. His son Asa succeeded him as king.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** And-he-removed ʾet-the-cult-prostitutes from the-land and-removed ʾet-all the-idols that his-fathers had-made.

**LOGOS (formal):** He put away the male cult prostitutes out of the land and removed all the idols that his fathers had made.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He expelled the male cult prostitutes from the land and got rid of all the idols his ancestors had made.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 14
**EMET (literal):** But-the-high-places were-not removed. Nevertheless the-heart-of Asa was complete with YHWH all his-days.

**LOGOS (formal):** But the high places were not taken away. Nevertheless, the heart of Asa was wholly true to the LORD all his days.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The hilltop shrines were not removed, but Asa's heart was fully committed to the LORD throughout his life.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-he-brought ʾet-the-holy-things-of his-father and-his-own-holy-things into-the-house-of YHWH — silver and-gold and-vessels.

**LOGOS (formal):** And he brought into the house of the LORD the sacred gifts of his father and his own sacred gifts — silver, and gold, and vessels.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He brought into the LORD's temple the silver, gold, and other items that he and his father had dedicated.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-war was between Asa and-Baasha king-of Israel all their-days.

**LOGOS (formal):** And there was war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Asa and King Baasha of Israel were at war throughout their reigns.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-Baasha king-of Israel went-up against Judah and-built ʾet-Ramah, to-not allow going-out or-coming-in to-Asa king-of Judah.

**LOGOS (formal):** Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah and built Ramah, that he might permit no one to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Baasha king of Israel invaded Judah and fortified Ramah to cut off all traffic to and from King Asa of Judah.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
